Reading

The innocent reading first. Asked for the foundation by name, the Overview gives its legal form, founder, scale, hosting, file formats, uses and the criticism it has met, from its own pages, Wikipedia, LinkedIn and the AWS registry.

Findings
  • THE FOUNDATION AT ITS GRAIN. '501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 2007 by Gil Elbaz' joins the home page ('Common Crawl is a 501(c)(3) non–profit founded in 2007.') to Wikipedia ('Common Crawl was founded by Gil Elbaz .'). 'Adds roughly 3 to 5 billion new web pages each month' and 'Cited in over 10,000 academic and technical research papers' agree with the home page ('3–5 billion new pages added each month.', 'Cited in over 10,000 research papers.'). The mission is LinkedIn's wording ('with the goal of democratizing access to web information'); the home page's is 'We make wholesale extraction, transformation, and analysis of open web data accessible to researchers.' The executive director the census row takes from Wikipedia ('Rich Skrenta is the executive director.') is not carried.
  • THE SIZE AND THE SPAN. 'Contains over 10 to 11 petabytes of data spanning nearly two decades.' The Overview page gives no figure: 'The Common Crawl corpus contains petabytes of data, regularly collected since 2008.' The home page the census saved: 'Over 300 billion pages spanning 15 years.' The first card, the same home page, summarises it as 'Over 300 billion web pages spanning 19 years'. The census row's corpus carries the saved page's '15 years'; the card and the composition's 'nearly two decades' count from the founding in 2007.
  • THE UNIT AND THE ADDRESS. WARC, WET and WAT ('Raw HTTP responses', 'Cleaned plain-text content', 'Metadata summaries in JSON format containing link and header details') answer the Overview page's 'raw web page data, metadata extracts, and text extracts'. The census row: a page 'is held by URL, with its metadata extracts and text extracts', with no author or attribution field; the composition names none, and its offer is 'how to query the Common Crawl index for a specific URL'. The crawl identifiers ('CC-MAIN-2026-43') and the Blekko list the crawl began from are not carried.
  • THE INTAKE GIVEN BY COMPANY. 'The dataset serves as a foundational training corpus for many modern large language models (LLMs) developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta.' Wikipedia: 'ChatGPT , as of 2023, was largely trained on Common Crawl,' 'as were other LLMs including Gemini', and 'In 2023, it began receiving significant financial support from AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI , each of which donated $250,000.' The donations are absent, and so are the refined datasets ('FineWeb, DCLM and C4'), which the census row gives as the place downstream where others make datasets from the raw crawl.
  • THE ATLANTIC'S FINDING THINNED. 'Because its scraper (CCBot) does not execute dynamic browser code or login scripts, it has faced criticism and pushback from news publishers and media organizations over copyright and paywall bypass concerns.' Wikipedia's account of The Atlantic's November 2025 investigation: Common Crawl 'misled publishers when it claimed it respected paywalls in its scraping and when it said that it was honoring requests from publishers to have their content removed from its databases', and 'It included misleading results in the public search function on its website that showed no entries for websites that had requested their archives be removed, when in fact those sites were still included in its scrapes used by AI companies.' The Atlantic's article is the fourth card ('Common Crawl Is Doing the AI Industry's Dirty Work'). The composition keeps a mechanism of the crawler and a concern of publishers; the misleading search results, which the census row reads as the limit of the index as a witness to inclusion, are absent beside an offer to query that index.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The foundation composed accurately at its grain from its own pages, Wikipedia and LinkedIn. The Atlantic's finding is reduced to publishers' concerns about how the crawler fetches pages, and the misleading index results, the census row's bound on the index as evidence of inclusion, are not carried.

[QUERENT] Common Crawl [SYSTEM] Common Crawl is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 2007 by Gil Elbaz that collects, preserves, and freely shares an open archive of internet data. [[1], [2]] Core Details & Scale * Mission: To democratize access to web information for researchers, educators, and developers. [[1], [2]] * Archive Size: Contains over 10 to 11 petabytes of data spanning nearly two decades. [[1], [2]] * Frequency: Adds roughly 3 to 5 billion new web pages each month. [1] * Hosting: Stored for free on Amazon Web Services (AWS) via its Open Data Sponsorship Program (`s3://commoncrawl`). [[1], [2]] Data Formats Common Crawl distributes its monthly crawls in three primary file formats: * WARC (Web Archive): Raw HTTP responses, including full HTML content and headers. [[1], [2]] * WET (Web Extracted Text): Cleaned plain-text content with HTML and code stripped away. [[1], [2]] * WAT (Web Archive Transformations): Metadata summaries in JSON format containing link and header details. [[1], [2]] Use Cases & Controversies * AI Training: The dataset serves as a foundational training corpus for many modern large language models (LLMs) developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. [[1], [2]] * Research: Cited in over 10,000 academic and technical research papers. [1] * Web Scraping & Paywalls: Because its scraper (`CCBot`) does not execute dynamic browser code or login scripts, it has faced criticism and pushback from news publishers and media organizations over copyright and paywall bypass concerns.
